observations:
Torah #128 is a three-line, single-paragraph teaching. It contains exactly one thematic cluster of concepts, all of which are already captured in Package 1 (הַשְׁפָּלַת הָעֵינַיִם וְעֵינֵי הַיֵּצֶר) proposed in torah_128_packages.json.

The teaching's entire conceptual content is a single bechina equation: blinding the eyes of the yetzer hara (כַּחְלִינְהוּ לְעֵינֵהּ דְּיִצְרָא) = the partially-righteous person suppressing his gaze (הַשְׁפָּלַת עֵינַיִם). The resolution — that the yetzer survives by looking sideways (מִסְתַּכֵּל מִן הַצַּד) — is the completing half of the same bechina, not a separate domain.

The only node deliberately excluded from the package is יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם (fear of God), which appears as a cause (eitza) of the eye-lowering, not as a bechina co-equivalent of any concept in the cluster. It is too large and cross-Torah a concept to be defined by its role in this three-line Torah; it is simply referenced here as the motivating force.

No independent second thematic cluster with 3+ bechina-connected concepts can be identified in Torah #128. The teaching lacks the structural complexity that would generate multiple packages. A single good/evil mirror is present within Package 1 itself (the positive act of suppression vs. the residual evil of sideways-glancing), but this polarity lives inside one package rather than across two separate packages, because the two poles are facets of the same conceptual act (suppressing vs. the surviving yetzer) rather than independent thematic domains.

Conclusion: Package 1 fully accounts for all bechina-language content in Torah #128. NO additional packages are warranted.
